offering.name: AccessGate
offering.purpose: Composable, default-deny authorization for Python applications with RBAC, ABAC, and lightweight relationship-policy support.

instructions: Use AccessGate to design and validate authorization policies, not to authenticate callers or infer permissions from unverified data. Prefer synthetic examples, preserve exact action and attribute matching, and require review before production rollout.

publicAccess.mcpEndpoint: dependency-free stdio server in the package and repository mcp/ directory

resources.name: overview
resources.title: Offering Overview
resources.description: What AccessGate does and where its trust boundary ends.
resources.content:
# AccessGate

AccessGate evaluates whether a subject may perform an action on a resource in a context. It supports exact RBAC grants, declarative ABAC conditions, tenant and ownership boundaries, custom policies, custom decision strategies, custom operands and locally scoped custom operators. It does not authenticate identities, verify tokens, secure sessions, or query application data.

prompts.template: You are helping a developer use AccessGate for: {user_goal}. prompts.template: Review this redacted AccessGate policy: {policy_summary}. Identify grants, deny boundaries, attribute provenance, indeterminate behavior, custom operators, sensitive metadata, tests, shadow-mode verification, and rollback.

acceptanceChecklist: Agents can distinguish authentication, session trust, and authorization.
RBAC, ABAC, and relationship-policy composition is documented.
Serialized ABAC policies are versioned and locally validated.
No operator uses arbitrary eval or implicit string substring membership.
Missing data and operator failures cannot be negated into access.
MCP tools do not require production identity or resource data.
Rollout guidance includes shadow evaluation, monitoring, rollback, and human approval.
